children: ITC shares traded higher while Happiest Minds Technologies extended losses on Wednesday, as investors continued to assess the proposed merger of ITC Infotech and Happiest Minds. Brokerages broadly see strategic benefits for the combined IT services business from greater scale, complementary capabilities and cross-selling opportunities, but remain divided on what the transaction means for Happiest Minds shareholders.

ITC was up 0.5 percent at Rs 268 in afternoon trade, placing it among the top Nifty 50 gainers despite a weak broader market. Meanwhile, Happiest Minds fell another 2.5 percent to Rs 353.65 after tumbling more than 8 percent in the previous session.

, the key debate is around valuation and execution risk. HDFC Securities Institutional Equities downgraded the stock to 'Add' from 'Buy' and cut its target price to Rs 400 from Rs 440, saying the deal valuation limits upside. The brokerage said the transaction offers no takeover premium to Happiest Minds shareholders, while the roughly 15-month integration timeline and uncertainty over retention of the existing management team pose risks.

Axis Securities took a more positive view on Happiest Minds, retaining its 'Buy' rating with a target price of Rs 415. It said shareholders could benefit from the stronger scale and diversification of the merged company, along with cross-selling opportunities across its larger client base.
Both brokerages’ target prices imply around 13-17 percent upside from Happiest Minds' current market price.

PhillipCapital's Karan Uppal also flagged uncertainty for Happiest Minds until the merger and subsequent listing are completed, potentially over the next one to one-and-a-half years. He said there was also limited clarity over leadership of the combined company, raising the possibility of management churn at Happiest Minds if ITC Infotech takes the lead.

, analysts see the transaction as a way to strengthen ITC Infotech without materially altering the investment case for the much larger parent. Morgan Stanley said the deal was small relative to ITC's overall market value, but could expand ITC Infotech's US presence, broaden its client base and improve its capabilities.

At the operating level, brokerages see benefits for both ITC Infotech and Happiest Minds from combining largely complementary businesses. Happiest Minds brings capabilities in generative AI, data, cloud, digital engineering and cybersecurity, while ITC Infotech is stronger in SAP, product lifecycle management, Industry 4.0 and enterprise transformation. The combined business would have more than 800 clients, with little overlap among their largest customers.

would become India's 11th-largest listed IT services company, with pro-forma FY26 revenue of about $791 million, more than 19,000 employees and operations across over 30 countries. Management is targeting more than $1 billion in revenue by FY28, supported by around 10 percent revenue synergies and a 100-basis-point improvement in margins.

The deal comes as India's $315-billion IT industry seeks greater scale and capabilities to navigate AI-led disruption in the software services market. Axis Securities said the transaction advances Happiest Minds' own $1-billion revenue ambition from FY31 to FY28 through the combination with ITC Infotech.

However, HDFC Securities cautioned that the margin benefits may take time. The combined entity's pro-forma adjusted EBITDA margin of 18.1 percent is below ITC Infotech's 18.5 percent, making the transaction mildly dilutive to ITC Infotech initially.

Under the transaction, ITC Infotech will first acquire a 22.1 percent promoter stake in Happiest Minds for around Rs 1,330 crore. Happiest Minds will then merge into ITC Infotech, with its shareholders receiving 25 ITC Infotech shares for every 81 shares held. ITC will ultimately own 73.4 percent of the listed combined entity.
